Indicator-based assessments of past and projected climate change, as well as its impacts on ecosystems and society, have been examined at both global and European scales (Metzger and Schr ter 2006, EEA-European Environment Agency 2017 ; Bednar-Friedl et al. 2022), also exploring the sensitivity to changes in climate and socio-economic drivers (e.g. Fronzek et al. (2019)). The European Council S 2014 Conclusions set emission reduction targets, with the approval of the 2021 2030 Framework for Energy and Cli- mate Change Policies (2030 Framework, MTMS 2021). In 2020, the European Council with a set of policy initiatives included in the European Green Deal endorsed a binding EU target, with the ultimate goal of achieving climate neutrality by 2050 and aiming for a 55% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 compared to 1990 levels, along with at least 32% of energy consumption from renewable sources and a 32.5% improvement in energy efficiency (European Commission 2020a, b; BOE 2021).

The reason for banning this type of flight is that although covering relatively small distances, they can still contribute significantly to greenhouse gas emissions due to the high fuel consumption per passenger mile. nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What is the main objective of the proposed policy in Spain regarding domestic flights?
nodes.answer: The main objective of the proposed policy is to restrict domestic flights on routes where a rail alternative is available with a duration of less than 2.5 hours to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and promote sustainable transportation.
nodes.paragraph: By delineating multiple scenar - ios, this study aims to offer a comprehensive exploration of the implications associated with the policy, thereby aiding in informed decision-making and policy formulation. The first scenario will exclusively analyze the prohibition of flights on routes with a rail alternative of less than 2:30 h, as the original text of the proposed ban states. It is worth mentioning that this time will be measured from city to city and not in travel time at the airport, as in the French case. Considering travel time from airports has created a paradox where flights to the same city, such as Lyon, may or may not fall under the policy depending on the Parisian airport of departure (Charles de Gaulle or Orly), even though the train alternative from Paris Gare du Nord station remains the same. Although the connection to Barajas airport is under construction and is expected to be available by 2026 (RENFE 2024), there are currently no high-speed rail con- nections to airports. However, several important routes are left out of this measure by a few minutes (Madrid-Valencia, Madrid-Sevilla or Barcelona-Valencia).

nodes.question: What challenge does the growth trajectory of the aviation sector pose for achieving sustainability in air tourism?
nodes.answer: The growth trajectory of the aviation sector indicates that without strong policy frameworks and lifestyle changes, achieving sustainability in air tourism will be an unprecedented challenge.

P rez Romero2,3 Martha Beatriz Flores Romero5 Accepted: 4 February 2025 The Author(s) 2025 Abstract Tourism in Mexico contributes to GDP and employment, but has environmental costs in terms of carbon emissions from air transport. The estimation of the carbon footprint of tourists arriving by air is crucial to raise awareness among decision makers in order to establish future tourism policies that reduce environmental degradation. This study esti- mates the carbon footprint generated by flights from three major Mexican tourist desti- - nations Canc n, Los Cabos, and Puerto Vallarta during the years 2022 and 2023. To carry out this research, official databases were used to determine the number of flights and the number of passengers visiting these places. Additionally, tools such as the ICAO carbon emissions calculator were employed to ensure accuracy in estimating emissions, considering factors such as flight distance, aircraft type, and passenger load.

nodes.answer: The growth trajectory of the aviation sector, combined with the lack of strong policy frameworks and lifestyle changes, presents unprecedented challenges to achieving sustainability in air tourism.

Global tourism growth averaged 4.2% per year in recent years (Bulin 2014), while the total con- tribution of travel and tourism to GDP was US$7613.3 billion in 2016 and is expected to increase to US$11,512.9 billion in 2027, indicating a significant overall increase (Hidayati 2018). However, this activity also generates a considerable environmental impact, posing seri- ous environmental challenges for societies, public administrations and corporate manag- ers. These are mainly through greenhouse gas emissions, with carbon emissions from air transport being highly significant, representing a major challenge in the fight against cli- mate change (Fleming et al. 2019; Lee et al. 2021; Mayer and Ding 2023). In fact, tourism is estimated to contribute approximately 8% of global CO emissions through activities related to transport, hospitality and trade in goods and services.

nodes.question: What challenges are identified in achieving sustainability in air tourism?
nodes.answer: The challenges include the ongoing increase in tourism emissions despite technological advancements, the need for strong policy frameworks, lifestyle changes, and the implementation of effective sustainable practices to align with climate targets.
nodes.paragraph: Air transport with 40% of total CO emissions from tourism contributes significantly to this footprint. According to the International Air Transport Association (IATA), the aviation sector contributes approx- imately 3% of global CO emissions, equivalent to 915 million tonnes of CO in 2019 (IATA 2020). According to Scott and G ssling (2022), long-haul flights are particularly important, which, despite accounting for only 3% of all flights, contribute up to 70% of the emissions of the tourism sector. In this context, it is crucial to quantify carbon emissions from air tourism, as it allows us to identify the main contributors to the carbon footprint and formulate effective mitigation strategies. The development of sustainable strategies in tourism is crucial to mitigate the environmental impact, considering that The International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) predicts that if no additional mitigation measures are implemented, emissions from commercial aviation could increase by up to 300% by 2050, due to increasing flight demand and industry expansion (ICAO 2021).
